'''Anders Björner''' (born 17 December 1947)<ref>{{Cite web |title="Festive Combinatorics in Honor of Anders Björner's 60th Birthday" |url=http://www.math.kth.se/bjorner60/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100207225848/http://www.math.kth.se/bjorner60/ |archive-date=7 February 2010 |access-date=19 October 2009}}</ref> is a Swedish professor emeritus in the Department of Mathematics at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]], [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]]. He received his [[Ph.D.]] from [[Stockholm University]] in 1979, under [[Bernt Lindström]]. His research interests are in [[combinatorics]], as well as the related areas of algebra, geometry, topology, and computer science.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anders Björner |url=http://www.math.kth.se/~bjorner/ |website=math.kth.se}}</ref>

His other positions included being director of the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Staff |url=http://www.mittag-leffler.se/organization/staff.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090404110621/http://www.mittag-leffler.se/organization/staff.php |archive-date=4 April 2009 |access-date=19 October 2009 |website=Mittag-Leffler Institute}}</ref> and [[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[Acta Mathematica]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Acta Mathematica |url=https://www.springer.com/math/journal/11511 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091115121548/http://www.springer.com/math/journal/11511 |archive-date=15 November 2009 |access-date=19 October 2009 |website=[[Springer Verlag]]}}</ref>

Björner is a recognized expert in [[algebraic combinatorics|algebraic]] and [[topological combinatorics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abstract of the CBMS Regional Conference in the Mathematical Sciences - Algebraic and Topological Combinatorics of Ordered Sets - 18–22 July 2005 |url=http://www.sciencestorm.com/award/0434402.html |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716015307/http://www.sciencestorm.com/award/0434402.html |archivedate=16 July 2011}}</ref> He is a 1983 recipient of the [[Pólya Prize (SIAM)|Pólya Prize]], and is a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] since 1999.

In 2025, he received the ‘Mathematics in Sweden Leader Award’.<ref name=R>{{cite web |url= https://research.com/u/anders-bjorner |title= Anders Björner |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Research.com |publisher= |access-date= 22 July 2025 |quote=}}</ref>  

By mid-2025, he had 120 publications and his [[D-index]] was 43.<ref name=R />
